audit.whatIsWrong: Level chart disagreed with the packet chart and with its own whys. Levels 4-5 and Level 6 were 'Skill' although whys[3] and whys[4] both describe Jax winning them outright, and 2+ items was 'Jax' although whys[6] says the threat shifts to a fed Nautilus off the lane.
audit.why: Packet levelChart is Skill / Jax / Jax / Jax / Jax / Jax / Skill at a 53.12% win rate over 3257 games. Nautilus has no dash, so once Leap Strike lands he cannot leave the trade — that is why 4-6 belong to Jax; late, his lockdown makes him a teamfight problem rather than a duel problem.
audit.corrected: phases[3]/win[3] Jax, phases[4]/win[4] Jax, phases[6]/win[6] Skill — matched pairs.

audit.whatIsWrong: Phase whys for Levels 4-5, Level 6 and 2+ items were generic boilerplate with no numbers.
audit.why: The real spike structure: Dredge Line is 14/13/12/11/10s, so a whiffed hook is a long free window; Depth Charge is 120/100/80s and is his only new threat at 6; Titan's Wrath is a flat 12s shield that has to be burst through.
audit.corrected: Phase whys rewritten with the actual cooldowns and the reason each stage sits where it does.

audit.whatIsWrong: Jax's ultimate written as 'Grandmaster at Arms' in whys[4], spikes[2].text and mid; the full layer already says Grandmaster's Might.
audit.why: Fabricated name rendering twice on one page. The genuine decisive interaction is also worth stating precisely: Counter Strike dodges basic attacks only, so it dodges Staggering Blow's root-auto and his follow-up autos, but Riptide is ability damage and lands through the dodge — the current text claims E dodges Riptide, which is wrong.
audit.corrected: Grandmaster's Might everywhere; Riptide corrected from 'dodged' to 'lands through the dodge, so the stun recast is the payoff'.

audit.why: Dredge Line's cooldown was already identified as the punishable window; it just lacked the number.
audit.corrected: 14s at rank 1 now stated in the Levels 4-5 phase.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Dredge Line's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Dredge Line is 14s at rank 1 — every whiffed hook is a free window, and with no dash he cannot walk out of the trade once you leap in.

edits.before: Grandmaster’s Might stats win every extended duel from here on. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Nautilus's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Grandmaster's Might out-stats a tank who cannot escape. Check Depth Charge (120s at rank 1) before you go — it is his only new threat here.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Nautilus carry threat 7/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: You still own the 1v1, but a fed Nautilus is an unkillable engage and peel bot — close it before teamfights, not duels, decide the game.

edits.before: Counter Strike online means you dodge his committed autos and Riptide, then recast to stun — he hands you the trade by walking up to auto.
edits.after: Counter Strike dodges his committed autos and the Staggering Blow root — Riptide still lands, so the value is the stun recast he walks straight into.

edits.before: Grandmaster at Arms' Armor/MR active and every-third-hit on-hit turn any all-in into a clean kill on an immobile target — just play around Titan's Wrath's shield.
edits.after: Grandmaster's Might's Armor/MR active and every-third-hit on-hit turn any all-in into a clean kill on an immobile target — just play around Titan's Wrath's 12s shield.

edits.before: Counter Strike is online: hold E through his Staggering Blow root-auto and his Riptide, then recast to stun and flip the trade in your favour.
edits.after: Counter Strike is online: hold E through his Staggering Blow root-auto and his follow-up autos, then recast to stun and flip the trade in your favour.

edits.before: Grandmaster at Arms — the Armor/MR active lets you eat his combo, while the on-hit passive every third strike turns the leap-in all-in lethal.
edits.after: Grandmaster's Might — the Armor/MR active lets you eat his combo, while the on-hit every third strike turns the leap-in all-in lethal. Depth Charge is 120s.

edits.before: This is your lane. Every trade is the same beat: Leap Strike on, hold Counter Strike while he autos and drops Riptide, recast to stun, then unload while he's locked. He's immobile apart from the hook, so once you're stuck to him he can't leave — just be ready for Titan's Wrath to shield his first few hits, so commit enough to burst through it. At 6 the Grandmaster at Arms Armor/MR active plus the on-hit passive makes a clean kill out of any all-in; just confirm his Dredge Line is down before you go, and respect that Depth Charge into a jungle gank chains perfectly.
edits.after: This is your lane. Every trade is the same beat: Leap Strike on, hold Counter Strike while he autos, recast to stun, then unload while he's locked. Riptide is ability damage and lands through the dodge, so eat it and take the stun. He's immobile apart from the hook, so once you're stuck he can't leave — just be ready for Titan's Wrath (12s) to shield his first few hits and commit enough to burst it. At 6 the Grandmaster's Might Armor/MR active plus the on-hit makes any all-in lethal; confirm Dredge Line is down first, and respect Depth Charge into a jungle gank.

edits.before: Level 1 is the only dangerous beat: Nautilus can land a Dredge Line hook and his Staggering Blow passive roots you on his first auto, so don't walk into hook range for a CS before you have Counter Strike to answer. Once you hit 2, Empower the landing hit of Leap Strike for a sharp burst trade he can't dash out of. At 3 the lane tilts your way — hold E through his root-auto and his Riptide, then recast to stun; he walks up to auto into a dodge window and has no mobility to disengage your follow-up.
edits.after: Level 1 is the only dangerous beat: Nautilus can land a Dredge Line hook (14s at rank 1, 1150 range) and Staggering Blow roots you on his first auto, so don't walk into hook range for a CS before you have Counter Strike to answer. Once you hit 2, Empower the landing hit of Leap Strike for a sharp burst trade he can't dash out of. At 3 the lane tilts your way — hold E through his root-auto and autos, recast to stun; Riptide still lands, but he has no mobility to disengage your follow-up.

notes: Two real defects beyond the level chart: 'Grandmaster at Arms' for Grandmaster's Might (three fields), and the claim that Counter Strike dodges Riptide. Counter Strike dodges basic attacks; Riptide is ability damage and lands regardless — that was in whys[2], spikes[1] and mid, and it would make a player mis-time the dodge window. Packet suspectNames (Titan's Wrath) were false positives.
